data.title: Visual direction for kadence
body: # Visual direction for kadence
- **Question:** how the landing page, the logo and the brand as a whole should look
- **Method:** 2026 trend scan (Tavily) + a teardown of the identities of four products in our category + the `design-color-system` and `design-typography-scale` skills
- **Rests on:** [landing page research](DOC-51), [the copy](DOC-25)
- **Status:** direction awaiting approval. Logo — three concepts, one recommended
## 1. What is happening in the category right now

**Technical Mono is already the default.** The 2026 trend reviews describe "code brutalism": monospaced typography, black-and-white or green-on-black schemes, ASCII ornament, the command line as an aesthetic. The description matches literally what any dev-tool team would do by default: "dev tools startups use mono logotypes and console aesthetics to look credible" ([Design Bootcamp](https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/aesthetics-in-the-ai-era-visual-web-design-trends-for-2026-5a0f75a10e98)).
The consequence for us is simple and inconvenient: **terminal aesthetics no longer signal "one of us". They signal "like everyone else".**
**What the neighbours on the shelf do:**
| Product | Visual strategy | Why it works |

| [charm.sh](https://charm.sh/) | The direct opposite of the terminal: "We make the command line glamorous", a pink-and-violet palette, jokes in the microcopy, every library with a character of its own | Tools for the TUI — and the brand deliberately does not look like a TUI. Which is why one screenshot is enough to recognise them |

| [warp.dev](https://www.warp.dev/) | SaaS pitch: "718K active developers", "51% of the Fortune 500", logos, testimonials | Works, because there is something to sell and someone to sell it to. We have neither — copying it would mean lying |
| [railway.com](https://railway.com/) | A wall of tweets from real people + product screenshots | The same mechanism: social proof as the main carrier. Out of reach at our stage |
| [bun.com](https://bun.com/) | One cream background, a pink bun logo, benchmarks as bars | The logo is literal and silly — and that is exactly why it is remembered |

**Conclusion.** Three of the four win not on palette but on having a language of their own. For Charm it is glamour, for Bun it is the bun. Copying someone else's language is pointless; we have to find ours — and we already have it, in the name.
## 2. The idea the name gives us
**Cadence is a musical term.** A cadence is the harmonic turn that **ends a musical phrase**. Not "rhythm in general" — the closing specifically.
The product's main action is `kadence sprint close`, after which a number appears. The coincidence is so exact that it would be a sin not to use it:
| In music | In the product |
| A cadence ends the phrase | `sprint close` — the moment the number is born |
| The repeat sign `|:` `:|` — "repeat the section" | A sprint is a section that repeats |
| A bar is an even unit of time | A point is the unit whose price we measure |
| A score — everything written down in advance and readable by anyone | The event journal — everything written down and readable without us |
This gives a visual language **no competitor has** and one that needs neither the terminal cliché nor an invented metaphor.
## 3. Three logo concepts
### A. The repeat sign — recommended
**Mark:** the repeat sign from musical notation — a thick vertical, a thin vertical, two dots: `|:`
- **What it means:** "repeat the section". Sprint after sprint, the same bar, measured
- **It types as characters.** `|:` can be typed on any keyboard, lives in the README, npm, `--help`, the TUI header and the command-line hint — with no image and no font
- **It works at 16 px.** Two verticals and two dots are close to all that is legible in a favicon at all
- **Monochrome by default**, colour carries no meaning
- **Risk:** not everyone will recognise the musical reference. Mitigation — it does not have to read as a note: the form stands on its own, and the explanation lives in the footer in one sentence
### B. Rhythm strokes
**Mark:** four vertical strokes of different heights — a bar, and also a velocity bar chart.
- Reads twice: as rhythm and as a chart
- **The risk that buries it:** every second analytics product looks like this. Zero differentiation
### C. Technical mono
**Mark:** the `kadence` wordmark in monospace, a cursor or a `$` beside it.
- Fast, safe, recognisable within the category
- **Risk:** it is exactly what anyone else will do. Invisibility instead of recognisability
**Decision awaiting approval: A.** B stays as the language for the section with the numbers (scales, bars), C is not used at all.
### Specification for mark A
proportions   height 24 u. · thick vertical 5 u. · thin 2 u. · gap 3 u.
dots Ø 3.5 u., at 1/3 and 2/3 of the height
minimum       16 px (favicon), 20 px in navigation
clear space   no less than the dot height on every side
colours       ink on paper, paper on ink, accent — on the dots only
ASCII         |:  — in the terminal, README, npm, TUI
forbidden     gradient, shadow, slant, rotation, any third colour value
**Wordmark:** `kadence` in lower case, always. Never "Kadence" — the command is typed in lower case in the terminal, and the brand must not contradict what a person types.
## 4. Palette
The ground is neither black nor cream. Black leads into the terminal cliché; cream with a serif leads into the look half the new sites have right now.
### Base
| Role | Token | Light | Dark | Why |
| Ink | `--ink` | `#12191B` | `#E8EBE7` | Almost black with a greenish lean — warmer than pure graphite |
| Paper | `--paper` | `#F1F2EE` | `#0F1416` | Cold grey-green, not cream |
| Surface | `--surface` | `#FFFFFF` | `#171D20` | |
| Stave line | `--rule` | `#D6D9D3` | `#283034` | Hairlines that divide the page |
| Secondary text | `--ink-soft` | `#4A555A` | `#9BA6AA` | 7.1:1 on paper |
### Accent
| Role | Token | Light | Dark | Rule |
| Accent | `--accent` | `#0E6E6E` | `#57B8B8` | Deep petrol. Free in the category: Vercel is black, Linear and Railway are violet, Bun is pink, Zed is blue |
| Metric | `--figure` | `#B4661A` | `#E0A15C` | Ochre. Its **only** use is the measured number the product exists for: `1.6h per point` |
| Verified | `--verified` | `#2E6B4F` | `#7FB495` | The evidence section |
| Not proven | `--open` | `#8A5A22` | `#C89A5E` | The honest-status block |

**The one-accent rule.** Petrol holds every interactive element. Ochre appears on the page **twice**: in the `sprint close` output in the hero, and in the same number next to the FAQ. A third time is a mistake: the moment ochre becomes an ordinary accent, the number stops being an event.
### Contrast
| Pair | Light | Dark |
| `--figure` on `--surface` | 4.9:1 | 6.1:1 |
All above 4.5:1. Terminal blocks are to be checked separately — that is where dev landing pages fail contrast most often.
**Colour blindness:** petrol and ochre differ in lightness, not only in hue. Statuses are duplicated in words, never carried by colour alone.
## 5. Typography

**The pair:** a neo-serif for headings + a monospace for data. The 2026 trend reviews name it outright ([Fireart](https://fireart.studio/blog/the-best-web-design-trends)) — and, more importantly, it works on meaning: the serif says "what is written here is honest", the mono says "this is a tool".
| Role | Typeface | Why this one |
| Headings | **Fraunces** (variable, `wonk` on) | A serif with character and a live detail. Not Inter and not Space Grotesk — both now read as "the default typeface for an AI-generated page" |
| Text | **IBM Plex Sans** | Engineering neutrality, sits beautifully beside the mono from the same family |
| Data, terminal, labels | **JetBrains Mono** | Native to the audience — they look at it in the editor every day |
Fraunces and JetBrains Mono come from Google Fonts, IBM Plex Sans too. Only the heading weight is on the critical path; the rest is `display=swap`.
### Scale
Ratio 1.25 (minor third), base 17 px.
| Role | Size | Line height | Tracking |
| Terminal and data | 14 | 1.75 | 0 |
| Labels (caps) | 11 | 1.4 | +0.1em |
**Rules**
- Line length 62–68 characters. A wider column kills readability faster than any typeface
- `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` everywhere there are digits — the "cost of ownership" table, the burndown, the sprint output
- H1 — `text-wrap: balance`
- Terminal blocks are **text, not an image**. They copy, they index, they weigh nothing
## 6. Composition: the page as a score
Sections are divided by **full-width hairlines** — stave lines, not cards with shadows. Content sits on the line, not inside a box.
- **One line, one thought.** A section can be read at a glance, without unfolding it
- **Cards only where there really are several objects** (three things a tab cannot do). Everywhere else — typography and air
- **A left column of labels** — the section number in monospace, like a bar number in a score. This is not decoration: it shows where you are on the page
- **Numbers have a weight of their own.** A measured number is never inside a paragraph — it is lifted onto a line of its own
**What this buys in practice:** a page with no cards and no shadows weighs less, paints faster and does not look like a template.
## 7. Motion
One orchestrated event, everything else static.
**The main one:** in the hero, the number `1.6h per point` appears 400 ms after the rest of the output — as though the command had just finished. Once, with no repeat on scroll.
Everything else has no animation: no reveals on scroll, no counters, no parallax. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` turns off even that single appearance and shows the final state straight away.
## 8. Brand carriers
| Carrier | What exactly |
| Favicon | mark A, 16/32 px, monochrome |
| og:image | the `sprint close` output on the paper ground, the number in ochre — no people and no gradients |
| README | the same block instead of a banner image |
| npm | wordmark + one line of description |
| TUI | the `kadence` header is already there; add `|:` before the name — one character, zero cost |
| asciinema | **a recording theme of our own in the brand palette.** Almost nobody does this, and it costs ten lines of config |
| Social card for Show HN | the H1 heading set in Fraunces on paper, nothing else |
## 9. What we do not do
- Green text on black. That is the aesthetic of 1983, which every second product now has
- An ASCII banner in the hero. In the terminal it fits; on the page it is noise
- Gradients, glass cards, glow
- Illustrations with people, isometry, 3D
- A logo shaped as a shield, a gear, a rocket or a brain
- A third accent colour
- Emoji as section markers
## 10. What to decide
1. **Approve concept A** (the repeat sign) or reject it in favour of B. C is not proposed.
2. **Check Fraunces on a real H1** — the variable `wonk` axis gives character, but it may be too much. The fallback in the same role: Newsreader.
3. **Who draws the mark cleanly.** The specification in section 3 is enough to produce an SVG in an hour; the only question is who does it.
## 11. Name collision — found 2026-09-04

The domain check gave a different answer from the one we were looking for. **Every** obvious variant is taken: `kadence.dev`, `.io`, `.sh`, `.app`, `.tech`, `.works`, `usekadence.com`, `getkadence.com`, `trykadence.com`, `kadencehq.com`.

One common cause: **[Kadence WP](https://www.kadencewp.com/)** — a site builder for WordPress (the theme, Kadence Blocks, Kadence AI), over 400,000 sites, owned by Liquid Web / Nexcess. The space around the name has been bought up defensively.
**What this costs us:**
| Consequence | Assessment |
| Organic traffic for the word "kadence" | Lost. The first page is WordPress, and that will not change |
| Confusion in the audience | Real: a web developer expects a WP theme behind that word |
| Trademark | The categories differ (WP themes against a CLI), but both are software. The risk is non-zero if the product grows |
**Decision (2026-09-04): the name stays, the domain is `kadence.tools`.**

> **2026-09-13.** `kadence.tools` was never bought. `kadence.guru` was registered through Vercel and bound to the site; the canonical address, the sitemap and Open Graph read it from `meta.url`. The consequences below do not change: SEO does not aim at the name, and diverging visually from Kadence WP is deliberate.
The main asset is the name `kadence` on npm, already ours. For a CLI that is a more important address than the domain: the main CTA leads into the terminal, not to a site.
**Consequences to account for in the work:**

1. **SEO does not aim at the name.** Queries: `git task tracker`, `sprint velocity cli`, `tasks in git repo`, `backlog.md alternative`. The word "kadence" stands first in the title only because that is what the command is called — not because anyone will arrive by it.

2. **We diverge visually, deliberately.** Kadence WP has a blue-violet palette and a rounded logo; our petrol with the repeat sign is not mistakable for it. That is an argument against any drift towards blue.
3. **Check again before the first release with a marketing budget.** If a trademark claim appears, renaming is cheaper when users number in the hundreds than when they number in the thousands.
